title.title: Foulkes' conjecture for $a = 6$, and quadratic stabilization
title.subtitle: Claim: $\mathrm{Sym}^6(\mathrm{Sym}^b V)$ embeds in $\mathrm{Sym}^b(\mathrm{Sym}^6 V)$ for every $b \ge 6$

plain: Two ways to stack symmetric patterns, one fits inside the other, now proved for size six

beats.text: Foulkes: one plethysm should embed in the other with $a$ and $b$ swapped
Proved one $a$ at a time, up to $a = 5$
The claim adds $a = 6$; Foulkes–Howe is surjective once $b \ge a(a-1)$

steps: Transposing an array of symbols gives a natural map
Once b is large enough, that map hits everything
Smaller cases are done separately: all of $a = 6$

achievement.label: Foulkes' conjecture (1950)
achievement.context: Claimed: the case $a = 6$, and the Foulkes–Howe map is surjective for all $b \ge a(a-1)$
achievement.note: The full conjecture, every $a$, is still open

verify.detail: Lean has the stabilization, and the case $a = 6$ only for $b \ge 30$
verify.ourCheck: We read the claim and the review; we did not check the proof

voice.text: Foulkes said one plethysm embeds in the other when a and b are swapped.
The transpose map is onto for large b; the small cases are done separately.
Claimed: the case a equals six.

sources.quote: Foulkes (1950); known a ≤ 2 (Thrall), a = 3 (Dent–Siemons 2000), a = 4 (McKay 2008 + Müller–Neunhöffer 2005 computation), a = 5 (Cheung–Ikenmeyer–Mkrtchyan 2017)
but the sixth-power case is formalized only for $b\ge30$
Only a = 6 for Foulkes (not the full conjecture).
